thread:
emma: FYI — after the roles_schema_v2 migration last night we started seeing 403s for a slice of support and billing users. Matomo shows ~72 failed requests between 02:12–02:25 UTC. I paused the rollout when I saw the spike. Anyone able to grab a quick signal? :eyes:
ryan: On it. first thing — are we sure the default role backfill ran? I remember the backfill job was hedged into a separate worker queue.
morgan: I ran a tail on the backfill logs earlier; there were a bunch of JSON parse errors around the role attributes — looks like attributes with empty strings got truncated. Could be the v2->v3 attr schema change.
emma: Ugh. That matches a couple of the support users — their role row exists but roles array is []. They should have had billing_viewer.
ryan: Quick check SQL I ran: 
```
SELECT id, user_id, roles, metadata->>'attrs' as attrs FROM role_assignments
WHERE roles = '[]' OR roles = 'null'
ORDER BY updated_at DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
morgan: Confirmed. ~46 rows returned with roles == []. Many have metadata.attrs like `""` or missing. Looks like the serializer collapsed empty attrs and the backfill treated that as an explicit empty role set.
emma: infra-bot — any deploy or KMS rotations around 02:00? Could a key mismatch have made the migrator write invalid blobs?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Chore: role-schema-migration rolled at 01:58 UTC on worker fleet-3. No KMS key rotation actions in that window. KMS logs: no decryption failures reported.
morgan: But in the app logs I saw this exception before the backfill wrote the rows: `TypeError: Cannot read property 'length' of undefined` in roles-serializer. Looks like an edge-case when attrs==null.
security-bot: /audit: I queried audit index for role modification events. There are `role_migration:update` events with status=success but payload shows roles=[] for many users. We should consider an automated repair and a DB-level safe backfill to restore default_role for users who lost all roles.
ryan: Proposed safe backfill snippet to run in a single transaction on replica then promote: 
```
WITH orphaned AS (
  SELECT id, user_id FROM role_assignments WHERE roles = '[]' OR roles IS NULL
)
UPDATE role_assignments ra
SET roles = jsonb_set(roles::jsonb, '{0}', '"billing_viewer"')
FROM orphaned o
WHERE ra.id = o.id
RETURNING ra.id, ra.user_id;
```
emma: That will set billing_viewer as the first role for ALL orphans which might be wrong for some teams. We should scope to users that were in support/billing groups via `user_org` or prior snapshots.
morgan: Good point. I have a nightly snapshot table `role_snapshots` from 2025-06-01 we can join against to infer prior roles.
ryan: Plan: 1) run join-backfill on replica to compute candidate updates; 2) sanity-check sample 50 users; 3) run repair in small batches; 4) resume rollout canary. Who can own the repair window?
emma: I'll own coordination and rollout gating. Morgan, can you prepare the join query and a quick sampling script? Ryan, please draft the ticket for rollback playbook in case the naive update causes regressions.
morgan: I'll have a sampling query and a dry-run update by +30 mins.
ryan: I'll stub a rollback playbook in incident board and add the kill-switch flags for the migrator.
security-bot: Recommend also exporting affected user IDs to a staging audit stream and kicking off an eval to ensure MFA & privilege checks still pass after repair.
emma: Agreed. Let's avoid a global default assignment without sampling. Will post results here when samples are ready. :thumbsup:
